summary: The four-gate acceptance loop is executable and enforced end to end, with evidence recorded at every step. All four required items are implemented and demonstrated: (1) a self-contradictory RESULT (status completed + INTERIM marker + not_run tests) is mechanically rejected at collect — CheckResultConsistency compares the completion claim against the document itself, requires a passed entry for every required test, and treats any not_run/failed entry as a contradiction; planted in e2e and refused with the not_run test named. (2) G2 runs CI's EXACT steps — gates.json holds the six jobs of .github/workflows/ci.yml verbatim and TestGatesSpecSyncsWithCIWorkflow fails the build on drift — and the merge gate asserts EVERY required job (TestCheckMergeGateRedScenarios subcases: no G2 record, subset G2 'the shipped defect', red required job, stale G2, non-ok collect, missing G3). (3) allowed_scope is validated against the real tree before dispatch — a glob matching nothing is a hard error, an all-dead scope refuses dispatch, and a task covering a marker input (specs/**) must also cover its derived marker (specs/SPEC_VERSION.json) — with the derived marker accepted at collect via the derived-artifacts rules. (4) A blocking red gate prevents merge, demonstrated: all four git/PR actions (commit, push, pr open, pr merge) exit 1 with REFUSED and the fake git/gh recorders prove no git/gh invocation while the gate is red; on green they run and write GitRecord evidence. The pre-dispatch gate-integrity defect is fixed: authoritative gate inputs (allowed_scope, baseline_sha, log path, guard files, settings) live in .rddev/runtime/tasks/<TASK>/gate-inputs.json — outside the Worker write envelope — and collect judges by them; a tamper Worker that edits its own task-package.json/registry.json is rejected with the out-of-scope file named. accept/reject/rework (same claude session)/respawn (new session, reset tree) work with rejection evidence kept; an independent Review Worker (no git control) records its verdict; rddev workflow TASK rebuilds the whole trail (state, G1-G4, rejection, review, git/PR) from disk alone and reports the exact resume command. An example task completes Worker -> G1 collect -> G2 -> G3 -> review approve -> accept -> commit -> push -> PR open -> PR merge -> merged, all steps with recorded evidence. Local CI runs: spec-validation, task-state, go, web and python jobs all green with their exact steps; migration-integration could not run locally (the worker guard blocks docker-socket access for this task and the contract forbids starting infrastructure) — CI provides the service container, and the G2 executor runs that job's exact step on the Supervisor side. 114 acceptance e2e checks (58 + 25 + 31) pass, plus the full Go unit suite, fmt-check, staticcheck and vet.

notes_for_supervisor:
Gate-inputs tampering (the pre-dispatch defect): authoritative allowed_scope/baseline_sha now live in .rddev/runtime/tasks/<TASK>/gate-inputs.json — a path outside the Worker write envelope. Spawn also snapshots byte copies of task-package.json, guard/worker-guard.sh, worker-settings.json and run-worker.sh; collect runs VerifyGateInputs (byte comparison) against the authoritative record and judges the scope/HEAD invariants by it. The worker-settings.json and guard files are therefore integrity-verified the same way: any edit is a tamper rejection, demonstrated for the package and registry by the e2e tamper worker.

Exit-status race fixed: the reaper wrapper now writes the authoritative runtime copy FIRST (program-order guarantee), spawn deletes stale exit.status copies from both locations at re-dispatch, and reconcileWorker waits for the reaper process to die (waitPidGone, 5s) before reading — fixes the attempt-1 flake where a reworked worker's stale exit status 0 was read for attempt 2.

Record timestamps are now millisecond-precision RFC3339 with mtime/name tie-breaks in LatestRecord and LatestGateRunRecord — fixes the flaky 'G1 is not green: no ok collect record exists' refusal when two records landed in the same second.

Git evidence files are action-qualified (git-commit-<run>.json, git-push-<run>.json, git-pr-open-<run>.json, git-pr-merge-<run>.json; record_type stays "git") so 'gate records' and the merge trail list each action distinctly.
